answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed when its actions are proven fraudulent, and its influence grows only through interactions with distinct counterparties whose own bonds remain intact. This makes identities costly to multiply: a sybil operator must lock real capital in every account and sustain convincing activity across a network, while coordinated accounts cannot cheaply validate one another. A gale of fabricated endorsements may look like a quill-marked fable, but it cannot recover slashed bonds or create independent counterparties.
